mgd.t: Direct indexing: losses harvested stock by stock
mgd.d: Owning the index companies directly lets the manager realize losses to offset gains elsewhere; a fund cannot pass its losses through. About $927 a year after the $672 manager fee (planning estimate).
Leave NVDA and AAPL out of the direct index and tilt away from information technology, so new money diversifies instead of adding to the concentration.
A tax-managed SMA takes IDX-I, NVDA, AAPL in as they are and sells them over time within the $18K yearly gain budget, instead of a one-time sale.
Rebalancing to the CIO allocation uses losses first, stays within the gain budget, and checks wash sales across the household's accounts.

mgd.d: Leave COST out of the direct index and tilt away from consumer staples, so new money diversifies instead of adding to the concentration.

Rebalancing to the CIO allocation uses losses first, stays within the gain budget, and checks wash sales across the household's accounts.
